title: Regular equations lift from a fibre for a flat finitely presented quotient
statement: Let $R\to A$ be a flat ring map [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map] of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], and let $I\subseteq A$ be a finitely generated ideal with $A/I$ flat over $R$. Let $\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}R$, $Q\in\operatorname{Spec}A$, and $P\in\operatorname{Spec}(\kappa(\mathfrak p)\otimes_R A)$ contract to $Q$ under $A\to\kappa(\mathfrak p)\otimes_R A$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Suppose the ideal $I(\kappa(\mathfrak p)\otimes_R A)_P$ is generated by a regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. Then there exists $g\in A\setminus Q$ such that for every model $D$ of the principal localization $A[1/g]$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away], the ideal $ID$ is generated by a $D$-regular finite list.

source.place: Tag 063W, lemma-fibre-quasi-regular, assertion (2), affine finite-equation form and proof by successive Tag 062Y applications.

proof.text: Let $F=\kappa(\mathfrak p)\otimes_R A$ and $L=F_P$. Each member of the given regular list in $IL$ can be written as the image of an element $f_j\in I$ divided by a unit of $L$. Indeed $F$ is a localization of $A/\mathfrak p A$, and $L$ is a further localization; use ideal membership in a localization and clear the finitely many base denominators. Multiplication of each member by a unit preserves every prefix ideal and every successive injection [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. Thus the images of the $f_j$ are a regular list generating $IL$.

Let J be the ideal of the lifted list and N=I/J as a finite A-module. Tensoring the inclusion I into A remains injective because A/I is R-flat [lem-weil-pbc-flat-quotient-tensor-injective]. After base change and localization at the fibre prime, generation of the fibre ideal implies that every element of the base change of N is killed by some scalar outside that prime, using [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact]. Apply Module.exists_notMem_forall_smul_eq_zero_of_tensor from the existing fibre-Cartier module, the finite-module Nakayama argument [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators]. It supplies t outside Q killing N, so tI is contained in J. Inverting t therefore makes the lifted list generate I.

Apply [lem-pur-fiber-regular-sequence-neighbourhood] to the lifted list to obtain regularity on A[1/g]. Let t be the multiplier from the finite-module Nakayama argument. Localize once more at t. Every element of I is now in the ideal of the lifted list, while the reverse inclusion holds because the list was chosen in I. Localization is flat (Mathlib flat localization and transitivity), so weak regularity survives. Since I is contained in Q and gt is outside Q, its extension remains proper; thus the list is regular [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. The iterated localization is A[1/(gt)] [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. Transport the list and ideal equality to any model by the canonical algebra equivalence.
